title: Code Nexus
note: Subject v2.1. The test scenario is yours: the script has to run without crashing, its title / wording is compared to the subject example as a warning only. The architecture is checked by importing your file: ABC with abstract validate / ingest and the signatures of the subject, validate() per type, ingest() raising on bad data, output() giving (rank, str) oldest first, DataStream methods and routing + stats replayed on the subject's batches, Protocol plugin + output_pipeline, CSV / JSON plugins. Source: imports abc / typing only, type hints, flake8, mypy (the subject expects a mypy error on the invalid ingest test of ex0: warning only there).

tests.name: validate(): each processor accepts only its own kind of data
code: n, t, lg = m.NumericProcessor(), m.TextProcessor(), m.LogProcessor()
cases = [(n, 42, True), (n, 3.14, True), (n, [1, 2.5, -3], True), (n, 'Hello', False), (n, ['a'], False), (n, log, False),
(t, 'Hello', True), (t, ['a', 'b'], True), (t, 42, False), (t, [1, 2], False), (t, log, False),
(lg, log, True), (lg, [log, log], True), (lg, 'Hello', False), (lg, 42, False), (lg, {'a': 1}, False)]
for proc, data, want in cases:
assert err is None, '%s.validate(%r) raised %r' % (type(proc).__name__, data, err)
assert got is want, '%s.validate(%r) should be %s, got %r' % (type(proc).__name__, data, want, got)

tests.name: ingest(): invalid data raises, valid data is stored item by item and output() gives (rank, str) oldest first
code: n, t, lg = m.NumericProcessor(), m.TextProcessor(), m.LogProcessor()
assert isinstance(err, Exception), '%s.ingest(%r) without validation must raise' % (type(proc).__name__, bad)
assert got == (4, '-1'), 'the rank keeps counting after earlier outputs: %r' % (got,)
assert all(type(g) is tuple and len(g) == 2 and type(g[1]) is str for g in got) and [g[0] for g in got] == [0, 1], 'LogProcessor output must be (rank, str): %r' % got

if got != [(0, 'NOTICE: Connection to server'), (1, 'ERROR: Unauthorized access!!')]:
note('log entries formatted differently from the subject example ("NOTICE: Connection to server"): %r' % got)

tests.name: a CSV plugin and a JSON plugin export the data as CSV / JSON
code: import csv as csvmod, inspect, json
cls = [c for n, c in vars(m).items() if inspect.isclass(c) and c.__module__ == m.__name__ and 'process_output' in vars(c) and n != 'ExportPlugin']
csv = [c for c in cls if 'csv' in c.__name__.lower()]
js = [c for c in cls if 'json' in c.__name__.lower()]
assert csv, 'no CSV export plugin class (a class with CSV in its name and process_output())'
assert js, 'no JSON export plugin class (a class with JSON in its name and process_output())'
assert err is None, 'CSV plugin raised %r' % err
cells = [x.strip() for row in csvmod.reader(out.splitlines()) for x in row]
assert all(v in cells for _, v in data), 'CSV output: the values 3.14, -1, 2.71 should be CSV fields: %r' % out
note('CSV output differs from the subject example (a line 3.14,-1,2.71): %r' % out)
assert err is None, 'JSON plugin raised %r' % err
return [s for v in d.values() for s in strings(v)]
return [s for v in d for s in strings(v)]
found = [s for d in docs for s in strings(d)]
assert docs and '42' in found and 'I love AI' in found, 'JSON output should hold a valid JSON document with the values "42" and "I love AI": %r' % out
if not any(d == {'item_3': '42', 'item_4': 'I love AI'} for d in docs):
note('JSON differs from the subject example ({"item_3": "42", "item_4": "I love AI"}): %r' % out)
